scheme_name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
content: Scheme Name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY / PM-JAY). Level: central. Applicable States: ALL_EXCEPT_NOTED_EXCLUSIONS. Description: undefined

scheme_name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
content: Eligibility rule for AB PM-JAY / PM-JAY: The applicant's household must appear in the SECC 2011 (or subsumed RSBY) PM-JAY beneficiary database, identified via rural deprivation criteria or urban occupational category. User explanation: PM-JAY is not something you apply for from scratch - the government already has a list of eligible families based on a 2011 household survey. You need to check if your family is on that list.

scheme_name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
content: Eligibility rule for AB PM-JAY / PM-JAY: For urban households, membership in one of the 11 officially listed occupational categories is one recognised path to SECC 2011-based inclusion. User explanation: If you live in a city/town and your main earner works in one of a specific list of jobs (like street vendor, domestic worker, rickshaw puller, construction labourer, etc.), that's one of the ways a family gets included.

scheme_name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
content: Eligibility rule for AB PM-JAY / PM-JAY: For rural households, meeting at least one SECC 2011 deprivation criterion (D1-D5, D7) or an automatic-inclusion category is one recognised path to inclusion. User explanation: If you live in a village and your household matches certain hardship markers from the 2011 census (like having only one room with a mud roof, no working-age adult, a disabled member with no able-bodied adult, being SC/ST, or being a landless labourer family), that's one of the ways a family gets included.

scheme_name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
content: Eligibility rule for AB PM-JAY / PM-JAY: There is no restriction on family size for benefit eligibility once a household is included - the Rs 5 lakh cover is a family floater with no member limit (unlike the old RSBY, which capped at 5 members). User explanation: However many people are in your family, they can all share the same yearly cover - there's no cut-off number of family members.

scheme_name: AB PM-JAY expansion for senior citizens (Ayushman Vay Vandana Yojana)
content: Scheme Name: AB PM-JAY expansion for senior citizens (Ayushman Vay Vandana Yojana) (AB PM-JAY Vay Vandana). Level: central. Applicable States: ALL_EXCEPT_NOTED_EXCLUSIONS. Description: undefined

scheme_name: AB PM-JAY expansion for senior citizens (Ayushman Vay Vandana Yojana)
content: Eligibility rule for AB PM-JAY Vay Vandana: Applicant must be 70 years of age or above, as recorded in Aadhaar. This is stated in the official parliamentary reply as the SOLE eligibility criterion for this scheme. User explanation: You (or the senior citizen you're checking for) must be 70 years old or older, and the age on record must match Aadhaar.

scheme_name: AB PM-JAY expansion for senior citizens (Ayushman Vay Vandana Yojana)
content: Eligibility rule for AB PM-JAY Vay Vandana: Aadhaar-based e-KYC is mandatory for enrolment and issuance of the Ayushman Vay Vandana card. User explanation: You'll need to complete a quick Aadhaar-based identity verification (e-KYC) to actually get the card - this can't be skipped.

scheme_name: AB PM-JAY expansion for senior citizens (Ayushman Vay Vandana Yojana)
content: Eligibility rule for AB PM-JAY Vay Vandana: If the senior citizen already holds coverage under CGHS, ECHS, or Ayushman CAPF, they must make a ONE-TIME CHOICE between that existing scheme and AB-PMJAY (Vay Vandana) - they cannot hold both simultaneously. This is a choice condition, not a blanket exclusion. User explanation: If you already have CGHS, ECHS, or CAPF health coverage, you'll need to pick one - either keep what you have, or switch to this new senior-citizen cover. You can't use both at once.

scheme_name: AB PM-JAY expansion for senior citizens (Ayushman Vay Vandana Yojana)
content: Eligibility rule for AB PM-JAY Vay Vandana: Holding active private health insurance or Employees' State Insurance (ESI) coverage does NOT disqualify a senior citizen from also availing AB-PMJAY (Vay Vandana) benefits. User explanation: Having a private health insurance policy or ESI coverage does not stop you from also getting this free government cover.

scheme_name: Central Government Health Scheme
content: Scheme Name: Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS). Level: central. Applicable States: ALL_EXCEPT_NOTED_EXCLUSIONS. Description: undefined

scheme_name: Central Government Health Scheme
content: Eligibility rule for CGHS: Applicant must belong to one of the officially notified categories of persons eligible to join CGHS. User explanation: CGHS is mainly for people who work for (or are pensioners of) the Central Government, plus a specific extra list: MPs, ex-MPs, ex-Governors, Freedom Fighters, sitting/retired judges of the Supreme Court, retired High Court judges, Delhi Police (in Delhi), Railway Board employees, and a few other named groups.

scheme_name: Central Government Health Scheme
content: Eligibility rule for CGHS: Eligibility for CGHS medical facilities is determined by the beneficiary's place of RESIDENCE being in a CGHS-notified/covered city, not by the employee's official duty headquarters. This list reflects cities notified as of the 2015-16 Annual Report; more cities have reportedly been added since (see uncertain_information). User explanation: You must actually LIVE in a city where CGHS operates - not just work for a job based there. The list of covered cities has grown over the decades and may have grown further since this data was last checked.

scheme_name: Employees' State Insurance Scheme
content: Scheme Name: Employees' State Insurance Scheme (ESI / ESIC). Level: central. Applicable States: ALL_EXCEPT_NOTED_EXCLUSIONS. Description: undefined

scheme_name: Employees' State Insurance Scheme
content: Eligibility rule for ESI / ESIC: Employee's gross monthly wages must not exceed Rs. 21,000/month for standard ESI coverage eligibility (see R_ESIC_002 for the higher ceiling applicable to persons with disability). User explanation: Your gross monthly salary (basic + dearness allowance + regular allowances, but not overtime/bonus) must be Rs 21,000 or less.

scheme_name: Employees' State Insurance Scheme
content: Eligibility rule for ESI / ESIC: If the employee is a person with disability (PwD), the applicable wage ceiling is raised to Rs. 25,000/month instead of Rs. 21,000/month. User explanation: If you have a disability, your salary limit for ESI eligibility is higher - Rs 25,000 instead of Rs 21,000.

scheme_name: Employees' State Insurance Scheme
content: Eligibility rule for ESI / ESIC: The employee must work at a factory/establishment covered under the ESI Act, 1948, in a district notified by the Central Government, employing 10 or more persons (in most States/UTs). User explanation: Your employer's workplace needs to have at least 10 employees and be registered under the ESI scheme.

scheme_name: Employees' State Insurance Scheme
content: Eligibility rule for ESI / ESIC: Coverage under the ESI Act applies to employees on an employer's payroll at a covered establishment; self-employed individuals, freelancers, and gig/platform workers not on a payroll are not covered under this Act. User explanation: You need to be a regular employee on your employer's payroll - self-employed people, freelancers, and gig workers without an employer relationship are not covered by this particular scheme.

scheme_name: Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme
content: Scheme Name: Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme (CMCHIS). Level: state. Applicable States: Tamil Nadu. Description: undefined

scheme_name: Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme
content: Eligibility rule for CMCHIS: Applicant must be a resident of Tamil Nadu. User explanation: You need to live in Tamil Nadu to apply for this scheme.

scheme_name: Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme
content: Eligibility rule for CMCHIS: The applicant's name must be present on the family/ration card used for household verification. User explanation: Your name needs to be listed on your family's ration card.

scheme_name: Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme
content: Eligibility rule for CMCHIS: CONFLICTING FIGURES FOUND ACROSS SOURCES: household annual income must be below a stated ceiling, reported as EITHER approximately Rs. 72,000/year OR approximately Rs. 1,20,000/year depending on the (non-primary) source consulted. NEITHER figure could be confirmed against an official Tamil Nadu Government Order or the scheme's own portal in this research pass. The numeric 'value' field is deliberately left as null so a rule engine does NOT silently apply an unverified threshold. User explanation: There IS a family income limit for this scheme, but our sources disagree on the exact amount (we've seen both about Rs 72,000/year and about Rs 1,20,000/year quoted). Please check the current limit on the official Tamil Nadu health insurance scheme portal or with the Village Administrative Officer before assuming you do or don't qualify.

scheme_name: Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme
content: Eligibility rule for CMCHIS: Certain notified special categories are reported to be covered under CMCHIS-linked schemes, in some cases without the standard income ceiling (e.g., differently-abled persons per SRC007). This could not be fully cross-verified against a single authoritative Tamil Nadu government source and may represent a distinct sub-scheme rather than a blanket exception within core CMCHIS. User explanation: If you're a transgender person, a person with disability, an accredited journalist, a Sri Lankan Tamil refugee, or an orphaned/rescued child, there may be a special path into this scheme (sometimes without the income limit) - but this needs to be checked directly with the Tamil Nadu scheme office since our sources aren't fully consistent on this.
